title: Put it together: inputs, outputs, and print
idea: Review the whole unit and tie input/output back to the print tool from Unit 1.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
exercises.explanation: Input goes in, output comes out, and print is how you make screen output.

exercises.prompt: Naming the input and output of a task is which UEPCC step?
exercises.explanation: U, Understand, means naming the input and output. You've been practicing it all unit.
print shows the text inside the quotes, exactly: Hi. The quotes aren't shown.

exercises.prompt: Task: 'Average four scores.' How many inputs?
exercises.explanation: Four scores go in. Count every value you start with.

exercises.prompt: Order the shape of any task.
exercises.explanation: Input first, then the work, then the output. Every task has this shape.

exercises.prompt: A program can run with no error yet still give an output that doesn't match the task.
exercises.explanation: Running isn't the same as being right. Always compare the output to what the task asked for.

exercises.prompt: Review: write a full program whose output is the word Hi.
exercises.explanation: print, brackets, the text in quotes: print("Hi"). You remembered your Unit 1 tool!

exercises.prompt: Task: 'Given a name, greet that person.' What is the input?
exercises.explanation: The name you're given is the input. The greeting shown is the output.

exercises.prompt: Which of these are TRUE about tasks? (Choose all.)
options: A task can have more than one input
You should name the output before solving
Inputs always come after the output
exercises.explanation: The first three are true. Inputs come BEFORE the output, so the last is false.

exercises.prompt: You finished Unit 2! What can you now do?
options: Name the input and output of a tiny task
exercises.explanation: You can now name the input and output of a task — the U of UEPCC. Great start! The other tools come later.
